about.title: About OpenOrgOS
about.lead: The full story — why we use an organizational EHR metaphor, what the protocol defines, and how open governance works.
about.ehrMetaphorBody: When care teams collaborate, they rely on a shared electronic health record: who the patient is, what happened, who delegated care, and a trail auditors can follow. Trade, partnerships, supply chains, and joint ventures need the same pattern at org scale. OpenOrgOS defines the protocol layer — Org Event Model, identity exchange, authority delegation, auditability — while committees carry local law and business rules.
about.whatIsBody: OpenOrgOS is a global protocol for inter-organizational communication. It defines the Org Event Model, identity exchange, authority delegation, and auditability. It is not an OS for internal HR, payroll, or intranet workflows. All business logic, legal interpretation, and organizational behavior are delegated to national or domain-specific committees.
about.openBody: Open in OpenOrgOS means incorporating the power and opinions of everyone who uses it — protocol proposals, reviews, standardization, and module development in an open community.
about.scopeBody: Trade between companies, university partnerships, NPO alliances, supply chains, joint ventures — any relationship where organizations must exchange verifiable state across boundaries.
about.visionQuote: OpenOrgOS aims to be the common protocol for organizations to communicate across boundaries.

learning.title: Learning
learning.desc: Setup guides, curriculum, and exams — learn OrgOS and OpenOrgOS in one place.
learning.orgosOverviewP1: OrgOS is deterministic software — the same inputs produce the same, auditable results. You operate it through LLMs and AI agents in natural language, so everyday organization work becomes easier without losing predictability.
learning.orgosOverviewP2: OrgOS supports work inside your company and communication between organizations. Start on-premises: board meeting minutes, contract management, and accounting / budget tracking — handled reliably with Skills and agent workflows.
learning.orgosOverviewP3: What OrgOS can do grows whenever you add modules. Install the modules you need and extend office procedures step by step.
learning.orgosOverviewP4: OpenOrgOS is built with AIA (AI Agent assistants) — our primary workflow, though Cursor, Claude Code, Copilot, and custom agents work equally well. Rules are Markdown/YAML; the reference CLI is TypeScript today, and Python, C, or other languages can implement the same protocol.

governance.title: Governance
governance.lead: Who can join, how committees work, and how roles grow.
governance.membershipOpenBody: OpenOrgOS welcomes Contributors, Reviewers, document authors, translators, and other community members broadly. Proposing rules, reviewing modules, and contributing code or docs is open regardless of specialty or region.
governance.membershipCrossBody: Committees carry significant responsibility for quality, merge approval, and standard adoption. When joining a committee outside your usual specialty, jurisdiction, or region, we apply clear criteria.
membershipCriteria: Demonstrated expertise in the committee's domain (accounting, legal, QMS, etc.)
Ability to understand and bridge the target jurisdiction, language, or regional context
Nomination by existing members or governance review of equivalent track record
governance.membershipExample: Example: A Japanese professional joining a China-focused module committee should have deep expertise in the same field (e.g. accounting or contracts) and be able to bridge rule differences between jurisdictions.
governance.promotionDesc: From Contributor to Committee Member — committee seats require expertise, nomination, and review.
